value: antennae of both sexes responded in electroantennography to every plant-volatile mixture tested, with varying amplitudes
method: electroantennogram (EAG) to binary and ternary mixtures of cotton and corn leaf volatiles, response relative to a liquid paraffin control and an n-hexane reference
conditions: Adults collected from cotton fields in Shihezi City, Xinjiang, China, and reared on fresh cotton leaves; field-collected adults of unknown age and mating status, which the authors say may have contributed to individual variation in antennal responses; only active, undamaged adults used, starved at least 4 h before testing; tests at 25 +/- 1 C between 10:00 and 20:00; six biological replicates per mixture, one antenna per beetle, no antenna reused; mixtures were tested in numerical order (not randomised), each in the sequence liquid paraffin, n-hexane, mixture, n-hexane, liquid paraffin; relative response A = (B - C)/(D - C) x 100%; females and males tested separately; 26 binary and ternary mixtures, each compound at its own optimal EAG concentration (10 or 1 uL/mL in liquid paraffin), 20 uL on filter paper; liquid paraffin negative control, n-hexane reference; one-way ANOVA with LSD post hoc tests (figure captions cite Duncan's test) and independent-samples t-tests between sexes; mixtures 4, 20, 22, 23 and 26 gave consistently strong responses in both sexes and the amplitudes differed significantly among some treatments; male and female responses did not differ significantly for most mixtures (p > 0.05), but differed significantly for mixtures 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 10, 11, 14, 15, 19 and 23 (p = 0.003 to 0.035, df = 10; 11 of 26 mixtures, including key candidate 23), and the text also lists mixture 25 (p = 0.090) among the significant differences

source.authors: Lun Li, Jiyu Cao, Zhiping Cai, Jing Chen
source.title: Plant Volatile Organic Compounds Attractive to Monolepta signata (Olivier)

quote: Both male and female antennae responded to all tested mixtures, with varying response amplitudes.
note: Licence: page metadata gives CC BY 3.0; Crossref gives CC BY 4.0, content-version vor, for the DOI (accepted pairing). Checked absent from main by species and DOI across the whole docs tree. Name and family/order as printed in the paper (Coleoptera: Chrysomelidae). Whole sentence read through a summarising page tool and confirmed unbroken under Results 3.1 (audit 324). The sex comparison is described as independent-samples t-tests but prints F values with df = 10. Caveats in the paper: the Abstract speaks of 13 plant-derived compounds while Methods 2.3 say nine compounds chosen from 14, and the text lists mixture 25 as a significant female-male difference although the p value given is 0.090. The quote and value say only that every mixture evoked a response in both sexes; they give no amplitudes and no ranking of mixtures. Behavioural (Y-tube, field) results in the same paper are not logged here.
